item.title: AG Marshall joins coalition standing with Florida to protect students from sexually graphic materials in K-12 schools
item.description: Attorney General Steve Marshall has joined a 21-state coalition of attorneys general in filing an amicus brief in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit supporting Florida's House Bill 1069 (HB 1069), which prohibits books describing sex acts from K-12 public-school classrooms and libraries."Over the past year, parents have used their rights to object to pornographic and sexually explicit material they found in school libraries," Florida Governor Ron DeSantis explained in a statement

item.title: Alabama oyster season ends amid sharp population decline
item.description: The Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources announced oyster harvesting season ends at 2 p.m. Tuesday.Alabama law requires the closure of all public water bottoms to oyster harvest to allow for proper conservation.The oyster season began on October 6. item.title: Multiple occupants severely injured in Opelika mobile home fire
item.description: The Opelika Fire Department responded to a mobile home fire early Tuesday, where they discovered four people with serious injuries.WTVM reported the fire occurred in the Oak Haven community off Marvyn Parkway. The mobile home was deemed a “total loss.”A man in his mid-30s was life-flighted to the UAB Burn Unit with severe burns. item.title: AG Marshall announces $150 million settlement with Mercedes-Benz over emissions fraud
item.description: Attorney General Steve Marshall on Monday joined a coalition of 50 attorneys general announcing a $149,673,750 settlement with Mercedes-Benz USA and Mercedes-Benz Group AG for violating state laws prohibiting unfair or deceptive trade practices by marketing, selling, and leasing vehicles equipped with illegal and undisclosed emissions defeat devices designed to circumvent emissions standards.
